params.body:
Closes #1063

## What was wrong

Two cars of a garage that imports through Hexon showed Car-Pass as "to register", although both had a valid Car-Pass in the garage's own Car-Pass account. A read of `carpass_requests` on production showed what happened on 2026-10-31:

1. The platform's observation got **ERROR 150**, "U hebt deze gegevens reeds meegedeeld": the garage had already registered that mileage itself.
2. The platform showed "Probleem gemeld" and offered a correction. Car-Pass answered all seven corrections with **ERROR 128**, "problem already solved or correction period expired". There was nothing to correct.

There were two causes:

- **Issue 150 was unknown to the platform.** Worse, the issue number was never read: production Car-Pass carries it as `issues[0].type`, and `CarpassIssue::describe` only looked at `id`, `issueId`, `code` and `issueCode`. Every issue came out as 0, and issue 131 could only be recognised by the words in its message.
- **The Car-Pass link from Hexon was dropped.** Hexon now sends `main.carpass` for both cars. For a partner that is not a premium trader, both `PUT update` and `POST create` on an existing car are refused as a whole (R P3-2.9, R P3-2.2), and the link went with the rest. A link that arrives after the car was created never reached `carpass_id`.

As a stopgap, the two cars were fixed directly in the database: `carpass_id` was set to the links Hexon sends.

## What changes

**Issue 150 asks for the link (R S3-3.10).**
- `describe()` also reads `type`, and maps 150 to a new action, `link`.
- `presentCarpassIssue` dispatches `carpass-already-registered`, and `carpassChip` opens a dialog with one field for the public Car-Pass link.
- `linkCarpass` attaches the link (`carpass_id`, `carpass_init = 1`) without a call to Car-Pass.
- The dialog appears both during the request and when the dealer clicks the "Car-Pass meldt een probleem" chip.

**A partner's Car-Pass link survives the refusal (R P3-2.14).** On a refused update, and on a refused create of an existing car, `CarpassLink::keepFromPartner` stores the link. It does so only when all of these hold:
- the car has no link yet, so an hourly resend cannot overwrite a newer report;
- the payload names the car's own chassis number, so a car matched on eight attributes does not get another car's report;
- the link is a Car-Pass report link.

No registration starts, and the answer to the partner is unchanged. The link is stored before the proposal (R P3-1.11) is recorded, so the proposal does not offer it again.

**Only Car-Pass links are accepted, on both paths.** `CarpassLink::normalize` takes `https://<host under car-pass.be>/vhr/<key>`, with or without the scheme, or the key on its own. Anything else is refused, because the link becomes the "Car-Pass" button on the public website.

New words are in nl, fr, en, de and es. The rules are in `13-s3-car-pass.md` (R S3-3.10) and `33-p3-integraties.md` (R P3-2.14, and a note on R P3-2.9).

## Not in this change

A car that has only a link and no stored report still gets a 404 on the PDF behind its Car-Pass chip in the list. That was already the case for every API car with a link (#658, decided for later).

## Tests

- `ACarAlreadyAtCarpassGetsItsLinkTest`, 8 tests: reading `type` and issue 150 in the production shape, the link dialog from the chip, attaching without a call out, refusing foreign links and other dealers' cars, the accepted link shapes, the three conditions for a partner link, and the real `PUT update` and `POST create` as a non-premium partner. Three of these fail on `main`.
- Full suite and PHPStan run locally; pint run on the new files.
params.title: Attach an existing Car-Pass instead of correcting issue 150
